note.question: How do agency versus reselling formats and the distribution of consumer valuations change endogenous product quality, prices, fees and the effects of upstream competition?
note.overview: The paper explicitly describes manufacturer-led Stackelberg games under agency and reselling formats and solves extensions with simultaneous upstream competition by backward induction.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

source.quote: Addition­ ally, under the reselling agreement, the intermediary opts for a reseller business that allows it to act as the middleman to resell the product bought from the manu­ facturer to consumers; for example, BestBuy.com offers a wide range of products from several brands and then resells them through its online marketplace.
In addition, Tian et al. (2018) study the strategic decisions of competing suppliers and a retailer to determine a more beneficial channel configuration.

sources.quote: A shift by manufacturer 1 from reselling to agency selling can be sustained as an equilibrium, and this also leads to lower product qualities and retail prices; in contrast, a similar move for manufacturer 2 cannot be sus­ tained as an equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In agency selling the manufacturer chooses quality, the intermediary sets agency fee, then the manufacturer sets retail price. In reselling the manufacturer chooses quality and wholesale price, then the intermediary sets retail price. Competition extensions add simultaneous manufacturer choices at the specified stages. manufacturer-led agency Stackelberg game manufacturer-led reselling Stackelberg game
